subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: When a connected IRC server sends an oversized record, should the account stay down, reconnect, or discard the record and continue?
rationale: The protocol permits closing, but the existing passive monitor does not establish how a deliberate post-ready close updates account status or recovers, and each option has different security and availability tradeoffs.

options.title: Fail closed with explicit lifecycle
options.body: Preserve the disconnect, propagate the terminal protocol error into account status, and make the chosen bounded recovery behavior explicit and tested.

options.title: Discard and resynchronize
options.body: Bound memory by discarding bytes until the next line terminator, report the violation, and keep the connection alive.

options.title: Accept manual recovery
options.body: Merge the current behavior with an acknowledged requirement that operators restart the IRC account or gateway after a violation.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with explicit lifecycle
recommendation.body: Preserve the disconnect, propagate the terminal protocol error into account status, and make the chosen bounded recovery behavior explicit and tested.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository explicitly assigns IRC ownership to vignesh07, making them the best available owner for the channel lifecycle tradeoff.
